article.title: Create, bind and rotate API keys
article.excerpt: A key proves which tenant is calling and which channels it may use. It is shown in full once, and a key with no binding cannot send at all.

p: A key is not just an identifier — it pairs a tenant with a set of permitted channels. The server checks both on every request, so a key is also the narrowest available way to scope what an integration can do.
Either header works; there is no difference in behavior between them.

steps.p: This page lists existing keys and their bindings.
The full value is displayed once, shaped sk_…. Store it the way you store any other production credential.
Select one or more channels the key may send over. Multiple bindings are allowed and are load-balanced.

p: Keys can be revoked and rotated from the console at any time. Because a key is bound to specific channels, rotating one is also how you narrow what a compromised integration is able to do.
list: A missing or invalid key returns HTTP 401 with code 40100.
A valid key bound to no channel is rejected with code 40000, not 401 — the key was fine, the permission was not.
Being bound to a channel that is not ACTIVE is also a 40000-class rejection.
